statements.t: Over the next five years, we plan to build and operate at least four more similar facilities in the United States.
We believe we are on track for completing all of our 2026 objectives.
We expect capital expenditures for each of our remaining facilities to be approximately $15.0 million, including recycling, product upgrading, power generation and expanded storage.
We have also announced plans to monetize our non-mining real estate, and water rights as soon as practicable, subject to market conditions.

We expect to explore the monetization of our remaining 35,662 Green Li-ion preferred shares once Green Li-ion experiences a liquidity event, subject to market conditions, most likely in late 2027 or 2028.

We expect to explore the monetization of our 2,000,000 common shares of Mackay Parent, that are contractually restricted until February 21, 2028, subject to its liquidity and other market conditions, most likely starting in February 2028 and continuing into 2028.

The Company intends to fund its operations over the next twelve months from existing cash and cash equivalents, proceeds received from the sale of the mining business, cash from sales from our solar panel recycling business, planned monetization of other non-strategic assets, and issuance of subsidiary-level equity (that is, by Bioleum).

Based on these existing and expected funding sources, management believes we will have sufficient funds to sustain our operations and meet our commitments and collateral requirements including the Great Basin agreement during the 12 months following the date of issuance of the condensed consolidated financial statements included herein.

While we have been successful in the past in obtaining the necessary capital to support our operations, including registered equity financings from our existing shelf registration statement, non-registered equity placements, non-registered equity issued directly from certain subsidiaries, borrowings, and various other means, there is no assurance we will be able to obtain additional equity capital or other…
The Company anticipates satisfying this requirement through a combination of third-party surety bonding and financial support from SSOF, an equity method investee of the Company.

SSOF is expected to fund the cash collateral or other financial commitments required to support the surety arrangements, potentially through note financing, and the Company expects SSOF to reimburse the Company cash funded in the escrow of $6.0 million.
The Company expects that the use of third-party surety bonding will reduce the cash collateral required relative to the maximum financial assurance amount.
The Company also expects that 20-year firm transportation reservation charges will commence in November 2028.
With the help of third-party valuation specialists, we estimated fair value using a probability-weighted expected return method.
During 2026, we granted Performance Stock Units that vest based on continued service and on our common stock reaching specified share price targets.

Because the share price targets are market conditions, we recognize compensation cost over the service period whether or not the targets are achieved, so the assumptions used at grant determine the total expense we recognize.

Payments under our 1.5% net smelter returns royalty depend on future mineral production from the properties, which may never occur and will be affected by metal prices, and Mackay may repurchase the royalty for a fixed payment.

Under the Precedent Agreement and a related guaranty executed on March 31, 2026 (the “Great Basin Guaranty”), we have guaranteed the performance of our obligations, including potential reimbursement of project development and default costs if the Precedent Agreement is terminated.

We are required to provide credit support through a phased surety arrangement collateralized by an escrow account, and the required surety amount is expected to increase to approximately $39.0 million by December 31, 2026 and approximately $54.0 million by December 31, 2027.
We expect to satisfy the remaining requirements through a combination of third-party surety bonding and financial support from SSOF.
If the Expansion Facilities are completed, we expect to be obligated for 20-year firm transportation reservation charges beginning in November 2028.

dropped.t: “We have now installed and tested substantially all our equipment, including front end loading and upgrades for offtake products, as we are near complete with our commissioning and look forward to continuous operations in August.
This represents four of the six-unit operations, and we now expect to complete the final two major unit operations prior to July month end.

“During the second quarter of 2026, we announced the successful sale, pending regulatory approval, of our legacy mining assets, with total consideration of over $45.0 million, including $20.0 million in immediate cash proceeds expected in August 2026, enabling us to redirect our resources and capacity on growing our industrial metals production and supply chain,” stated Corrado De Gasperis.

Our entire Board is highly cognizant of our cash positions and share price, and we aim to deploy cash carefully and judiciously towards delivering maximum shareholder value by monetizing non-core assets and using non-dilutive funding for metals.”

“Our solar recycling facility will be up and running in August and operate at least 25% of rated capacity from then through year end, if not higher, generating an expected $5 million in revenues in the second half of 2026,” concluded Mr.
Unaddressed questions will be reviewed by management and responded to accordingly.
